course.title: Java — Complete Deep Learning Course
course.description: A genuinely Java-specific, beginner-to-advanced course with concept-first notes, practical coding, dedicated tasks, testing and a complete capstone.
course.curriculumPolicy: Module and lesson counts are determined by the concepts required to learn this language properly; no fixed module/lesson template is imposed.
learningOutcomes: Understand Java from fundamentals to advanced practical programming.

modules.title: Java Foundations
modules.description: JDK/JVM concepts, program structure, primitive types and execution.

lessons.title: Java Foundations
lessons.description: JDK/JVM concepts, program structure, primitive types and execution.
learningObjectives: Understand the mental model behind Java Foundations.
Write correct Java code using Java Foundations.
Explain the program flow in your own words.
Handle at least one edge case.
Apply the concept in a practical task.

notes.text: JDK/JVM concepts, program structure, primitive types and execution.

In this lesson, the student should understand java foundations before trying to memorize syntax. Start with the mental model, then connect each rule to a small program and finally to the practical task.
Java Foundations is important because it appears repeatedly when building real Java programs. A student should be able to explain when to use it, what can go wrong, and how to test the result.

notes.caption: Create a teaching diagram showing the relationship between the main ideas in Java Foundations.

items: Define the main idea behind Java Foundations.
Understand the syntax or API involved.
Trace what happens step by step when the program runs.
Know the common failure cases.
Choose a clear and maintainable implementation.

notes.text: Read the example from top to bottom. Predict the result first. Then run it and compare your prediction with the actual result.

notes.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) { System.out.println("Hello, Java"); } }

items: Identify the input or starting state.
Identify the important variables/data structures.
Follow each operation in order.
Observe the output or returned value.
Ask what would happen with invalid, empty, very large or unexpected input.
Copying syntax without understanding the data flow.
Ignoring invalid input or boundary cases.
Mixing responsibilities into one large function.
Failing to test the code after changing it.
Using a more complex technique when a simpler one is clearer.
Prefer readable names and small responsibilities.
Validate assumptions at boundaries.
Keep repeated logic reusable.
Test both expected and failure paths.
Use the official language documentation when behavior is uncertain.
I can explain Java Foundations without reading the notes.
I can write a small example from memory.
I can identify at least one edge case.
I can explain one common mistake and how to avoid it.

practicals.title: Guided Practical — Java Foundations
practicals.objective: Use Java Foundations in a small but complete Java exercise.
steps: Change the input and predict the result.
Test an invalid or boundary case.
practicals.starterCode: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) { System.out.println("Hello, Java"); } }
practicals.expectedOutput: A working Java program demonstrating Java Foundations.

tasks.title: Dedicated Task — Java Foundations
tasks.description: Build a command-line student welcome program.
requirements: The solution must demonstrate Java Foundations.
Use clear naming and structure.
Validate relevant input.
Handle at least two edge cases.
Include a short README explaining the approach.
acceptanceCriteria: Student can explain the important code.

quiz.question: Which statement best describes Java Foundations?
options: It is a core Java programming concept covered in this lesson.
It is only a CSS feature.
quiz.answer: It is a core Java programming concept covered in this lesson.
